draft.title: Non-ohmic devices
card: Ohmic
a device whose resistance stays constant, so current is directly proportional to voltage. Its I-V graph is a straight line through the origin.
Non-ohmic
a device whose resistance changes as the voltage or conditions change. Its I-V graph is a curve, or a line that is not straight.
Diode and LED
these let current flow easily in one direction only. An LED is a diode that gives off light. Little current flows until the voltage passes a certain value, then the current rises steeply.
Thermistor and LDR
a thermistor changes resistance with temperature. A light dependent resistor (LDR) changes resistance with light level. For a typical LDR, resistance falls as light gets brighter.
draft.remember: If the I-V graph is not a straight line through the origin, the device is non-ohmic.

a.q: The I-V graph of a component is a curve. What does this show about the component?
opts: Its resistance changes, so it is non-ohmic
Its resistance is constant, so it is ohmic
Its current stays the same at every voltage
It lets current flow in both directions equally
a.why: A curved I-V graph means the ratio of voltage to current is not constant, so the resistance changes and the device is non-ohmic. A constant resistance would give a straight line through the origin.
a.clue: What shape is the graph for a device with constant resistance?

b.q: Sam builds a night light for a hallway in Geelong. It must switch on when the room gets dark. Which component changes its resistance with light level?
opts: A light dependent resistor
A thermistor
A diode
A fixed resistor
b.why: A light dependent resistor changes resistance with light level, so it can sense when the room gets dark. A thermistor is the most tempting wrong choice, but it responds to temperature, not light.
b.clue: Which component responds to light, not heat?

a.best: Its resistance changes, so it is non-ohmic

problems.detail: The non-ohmic definition says the graph is 'a curve, or a line that is not straight', which is redundant. It also leaves out the case of a straight line that does not pass through the origin, which the remember line and the ohmic definition cover. Better: 'Its I-V graph is not a straight line through the origin.'

The question asks which component 'changes its resistance with light level', which matches the option name 'light dependent resistor' word for word. The clue ('responds to light, not heat') gives the answer away further. A student can pick it without understanding, so the question is too easy for Year 11.

check.summary: Facts are correct and both answers are clear. The card's non-ohmic definition is worded redundantly and leaves out straight lines that miss the origin, and question b gives its answer away by matching 'light level' to 'light dependent resistor'.

3.alt: Current against voltage for a resistor and a diode. The resistor's graph is a straight line through the origin, so it is ohmic. The diode carries almost no current when connected the other way (negative voltage) and very little at first the right way round, then the current rises steeply once the voltage passes about 0.6 V, so it is non-ohmic.
